// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

blocks.text:
# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:24:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

blocks.text:
# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:24:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1776._

> ℹ️ **4 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/config/config_service.dart` line 80

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 885

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

---

### Thread 7 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart` line 200

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch

Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a

fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-Zz` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:480`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-a2` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:977`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-cZ` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:995`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-dl` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:305`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-fJ` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:885`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-gR` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:200`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch
re-creates all three as `io`/`cleanEnv`/`cleanRoot` with identical expressions.
Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a
`--cwd` handling the other forgets). Same for the `FileSessionPresenceStore`
wiring, which is copied verbatim from the repair branch.

# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:24:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

blocks.text:
# gh-1746: [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)

## Description

## Goal — Session disk hygiene (v2 — revised framing)

One sentence: **the sessions root gets an opt-in retention policy (`sessions.retention`) — a total-size cap enforced by an age-aware, live/named-safe sweep at boot — so a workspace of marathon sessions can never quietly eat the disk, while with no config nothing is EVER auto-deleted.**

Today nothing bounds the sessions root: a single marathon workspace holds 425 MB + 4.8 GB transcripts (measured, dmtools slug), macOS has already throttled fa for 8.6 GB of dirty writes in 15 h (YuryBY's #1745 diag log). The only tools are manual: `fa session repair` shrinks a ledger, `delete` removes one session, `cleanupEmptySessions` removes EMPTY files. There is no cap, no sweep, no usage visibility beyond `/sessions` listing.

## Why this framing

- **v1 of this issue ("configurable full-open bound") is RETRACTED as the framing** — it answered a memory-risk question (how big a file may be fully opened), not the owner's actual ask (stop sessions filling the disk). The full-open knob stays a legitimate second-tier follow-up, listed under Non-goals.
- "Auto-clean by default" is rejected as the default posture: silently deleting session history is the one irreversible action fa must never take unconfigured. Opt-in cap (variant B below) is the recommendation; the alternative (default cap) is an explicit open question for the owner.

## Architecture

Named components:

- **Config** (user file, tolerant section — unknown keys note, never boot-fail):
  ```yaml
  sessions:
    retention:
      maxTotalBytes: 0      # 0/absent = NO cap, nothing is ever auto-deleted (default)
      minAgeDays: 14        # a session younger than this is never swept
      keepNamed: true       # named sessions (--session <name>) are always exempt
      sweep: boot           # boot | off — when the sweep runs (off = cap set but manual-only)
  ```
- **Usage walk** — O(directory entries), never O(file bytes): stat-based size + last-used (mtime; a live presence marker overrides recency), reusing the header-only listing the picker already streams.
- **Sweep** (`SessionRetentionSweeper`, pure-Dart core over `ExecutionEnv`): when total > `maxTotalBytes`, delete oldest-last-used first until under the cap, skipping: live sessions (presence file), named sessions (`keepNamed`), anything younger than `minAgeDays`, and the CURRENT session. Every deletion logs one line (file, size, age, reason). If the exempt set alone exceeds the cap, STOP and emit a loud note naming the blockers — never force.
- **Session-owned artifacts die with the session**: the transcript JSONL plus its sidecars in the same sweep unit — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml`, `spills/<sessionId>/`, trajectory blobs `<sid>/`. Presence files are garbage-collected separately (they are not user data; #1660/#1740 already touched them).
- **Visibility**: `/sessions` gains a usage footer (`total X GB across N sessions, cap Y`); `fa sessions clean [--dry-run]` runs the sweep manually with a full report (what would be / was deleted, freed bytes, exemptions).
- Degradation: absent section = byte-identical today; a cap set but unreachable exemptions = note, no deletion loop.

## Capability surface

| Surface | Today | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Total disk cap | none | `maxTotalBytes`, opt-in |
| Auto-delete | none (manual delete only) | boot sweep, oldest-first, exempt live/named/young |
| Manual verb | `fa session repair`, per-file delete | `fa sessions clean --dry-run` + apply |
| Usage visibility | `/sessions` list only | total + per-slug + cap footer |
| Sidecar cleanup | none | dies with its session |

Tiering: **core** = config + sweeper + `fa sessions clean` + `/sessions` footer; **second tier** = app Settings surface, Trash-style archive instead of delete (`retention.archive: true` moves to `.fah/trash/`); **excluded** — spills/bash-jobs GLOBAL caps (their own growth has separate cards; only session-scoped subdirs ride this sweep), and any compaction of LIVE sessions (repair owns that).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — no `sessions:` section → no sweep ever runs, no boot note (byte-identical legacy; UT on config).
- **AC2** — cap set, total under → no deletions (UT).
- **AC3** — cap set, total over → oldest-last-used deleted until under; deleted set excludes live (presence), named (`keepNamed: true`), younger than `minAgeDays`, and the current session (IT with fake fs + fake clock).
- **AC4** — exempt-only overflow: nothing deleted, loud note names each blocker with size (UT).
- **AC5** — deleting a session removes its sidecars (`.tools/`, `spills/<sid>/`, trajectory blobs) in the same unit (IT).
- **AC6** — `fa sessions clean --dry-run` prints the exact plan (paths, sizes, ages, reasons) and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly the plan (E2E).
- **AC7** — every auto-deletion emits one log line; a sweep report persists to the boot log (IT asserts the lines).

## Test plan

- `UT-1..2` — config parse (absent/invalid/zero/valid) → AC1/2.
- `UT-3` — sweeper selection order + exemptions on a synthetic tree (AC3/4).
- `IT-1` — fake `ExecutionEnv` + fake clock: full sweep lifecycle incl. sidecars (AC3/5), log lines (AC7).
- `IT-2` — named/live/young exemption matrix (AC3).
- `E2E-1` — real fs temp root: `fa sessions clean --dry-run` then apply; `/sessions` footer numbers (AC6).
- `REG-1` **merge-blocking**: legacy-config fixture (no section) — no sweep, no notes, `/sessions` output byte-identical modulo the new footer line being ABSENT without a cap. **A red REG-1 job blocks merge even when all IT/E2E are green.**
- `REG-2` — presence/named sessions survive every sweep shape (property test over generated trees).

### Edge / border cases

- **E1** — cap smaller than one marathon session: that session is still a deletion candidate (oldest-first) unless exempt — minAgeDays is the guard, not size.
- **E2** — race: a session becomes live mid-sweep → presence check immediately before each unlink; skip on mismatch.
- **E3** — clock skew / mtime touch by backup tools → last-used falls back to header `updatedAt` when mtime < header time.
- **E4** — symlinked session root: never follow links out of the root (path-escape test).
- **E5** — `sweep: off` with cap set: manual verb still works, boot never sweeps (only the over-cap note).
- **E6** — cross-slug fairness: cap is global across all project slugs; no slug starvation (oldest wins globally).

## Non-goals

- No default cap / no surprise deletion ever (that is the framing, restated as a guarantee).
- No live-session compaction/repair inside the sweep (`fa session repair` owns shrinking).
- No spills/bash-jobs global quotas — session-scoped subdirs only.
- The retracted v1 full-open knob (`sessions.maxFullOpenBytes`) — separate follow-up if wanted.
- No cloud/archive backend.

## Open questions

1. Default posture: **B (recommended)** — no cap unless set, boot NOTE (no action) when total crosses a soft warn threshold (e.g. 5 GiB) suggesting the keys; or **A** — ship a generous default cap (e.g. 20 GiB) with the same exemptions, so hygiene exists out of the box. Owner decides.
2. Delete vs archive-to-`.fah/trash/` for auto-swept sessions (manual verb always hard-deletes): recommend archive as second tier, delete for core.

## References

- Measured: dmtools slug 425 MB live + 4.8 GB kimi transcript; macOS throttle diag in #1745.
- Code: `session_repo.dart:413` (`cleanupEmptySessions` — empties only), `session_commands.dart` (manual delete), no retention anywhere (`grep retention|prune` — nothing).
- Related: #1745 (ledger growth — the producer side; this card is the consumer side), gh-1073/#1247 (per-record caps), #1590/#1594 (snapshot ledgers), #919 (bash_jobs log growth — adjacent, excluded here).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1776
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1776
- **Title**: gh-1746 [GOAL] Session disk hygiene: opt-in retention cap + age-aware sweep (nothing auto-deleted unless configured)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1746` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 18
- **Additions**: +2357
- **Deletions**: -5
- **Created**: 2026-10-21T22:10:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-22T00:24:01Z

## PR Description

Closes #1746
### What changed
Added the opt-in `sessions.retention` policy (gh-1746): a total-size cap enforced at boot by an age-aware sweep that deletes whole session units (transcript, segments, `.tools`, usage dir, spills) oldest-last-used-first, exempting live (presence), named, and young sessions. Without the config section nothing ever runs — byte-identical legacy boot.

### Key decisions
- New `lib/src/session_retention.dart` — pure Dart over `FileSystem` (MemoryExecutionEnv-testable), stat-first usage walk, fail-closed: a presence probe failure aborts the sweep instead of risking a live session
- Boot seam: `_retentionBootCheck()` awaited in `_initializeSession()` before any session opens; report lines go to fa.log (`[retention]`) and the dim notice channel (line mode + TUI re-print)
- Tolerant config like `spills:` — unknown keys/mistyped scalars become notes, never boot failures; `CliConfig` round-trips the section (defaults never written)
- Manual verb `fa session clean [--dry-run]` (AC6): dry run prints the exact plan and deletes nothing; apply performs exactly that plan; `sweep: off` makes this the only enforcement path
- Posture B soft warn: 5 GiB threshold emits one no-action boot note suggesting the keys (only when the section is touched)

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/session_retention_test.dart test/session_retention_config_test.dart test/cli/session_clean_cli_test.dart
```
E2E: `HOME=<tmp> fa session clean --dry-run` with a `sessions.retention.maxTotalBytes` cap in `$HOME/.fah/config.yaml` — plan prints, nothing deletes; re-run without `--dry-run` to apply.

Note: `headless_log_file_test` and `yolo_rm_critical_e2e_test` (spawn-based E2Es that pick up the runner's real provider queue) fail on clean `origin/main` too — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  CFG["~/.fah/config.yaml sessions.retention"] --> CC["CliConfig (tolerant)"]
  CC --> AC["AgentCliConfig.sessionsRetention"]
  AC --> BOOT["_retentionBootCheck() in _initializeSession"]
  BOOT --> SW["SessionRetentionSweeper.enforceAtBoot"]
  SW -->|"plan: oldest-first, exempt live/named/young"| DEL["delete whole units (re-check presence per unlink)"]
  SW --> LOG["fa.log [retention] lines + dim boot notice"]
  CLI2["fa session clean [--dry-run]"] --> SW
```

</details>

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

---

### Thread 2 — `lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` line 480

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

---

### Thread 3 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 977

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 995

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 305

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-22):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a

the unused surface.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/session_retention.dart` line 885

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

## New Comments & Review Threads (29)

### 1. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-YJ` — **unknown** (`lib/src/config/config_service.dart:80`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: parity completeness gate is red — the new `sessions` yaml key is unclassified**

`dart test test/parity/settings_completeness_test.dart` on this head fails (2 tests):

```
❌ every parsed yaml key is classified
Expected: empty
  Actual: ['sessions']
Unclassified yaml keys: [sessions]. Every top-level key the parsers read
must be owned by a SharedSetting (yamlKeyCoverage) or listed in
fileOnlyConfigKeys with a WHY.

❌ the audit table covers every key exactly once
```

This PR adds `'sessions'` to `configTopLevelKeys` (this line) and reads
`map['sessions']` in `CliConfig.fromYaml`, but `lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart`
is untouched: `sessions` is in neither a `SharedSetting.yamlKeys` nor
`fileOnlyConfigKeys`, so the completeness ratchet (AGENTS.md parity rules:
"A new yaml key landing without a classification is RED") fails — this blocks the
SM pre-merge validation.

Fix (one entry, matching the SKILL.md `<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->`
intent):

```dart
// lib/src/parity/settings_registry.dart, fileOnlyConfigKeys:
'sessions':
    'Session retention (gh-1746) is boot-time disk hygiene for the '
    'CLI-owned sessions root; no app surface edits it interactively.',
```

Run `dart test test/parity/` after classifying.

### 2. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-Zz` — **unknown** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart:480`)

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-a2` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:977`)

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-cZ` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:995`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-dl` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:305`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-fJ` — **unknown** (`lib/src/session_retention.dart:885`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6u_-gR` — **unknown** (`bin/fah_runapp.dart:200`)

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch
re-creates all three as `io`/`cleanEnv`/`cleanRoot` with identical expressions.
Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a
`--cwd` handling the other forgets). Same for the `FileSessionPresenceStore`
wiring, which is copied verbatim from the repair branch.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the boot seam itself has zero test coverage (AC7's log wiring, boot ordering, REG-1, E2E-1)**
