### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e9216f9a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch

Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e9216f9a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch
re-creates all three as `io`/`cleanEnv`/`cleanRoot` with identical expressions.
Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a
`--cwd` handling the other forgets). Same for the `FileSessionPresenceStore`
wiring, which is copied verbatim from the repair branch.

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.

   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

## New Comments & Review Threads (37)

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate

670-            '      \'---\\nname: self-settings\\ndescription: >\\n  Configure fa (flutter_agent_harness) itself by editing the exact config\\n  files the CLI settings commands write: provider/model selection and roles,\\n  memory paths, tool availability, cubes, MCP servers, redaction, skills\\n  access, approval and mode, themes and TUI appearance (tui.theme: switch\\n  or create a theme). Use when asked to reconfigure fa without a human\\n  in the REPL ("switch us to provider X", "point project memory at this\\n  path", "disable web_search for this project", "switch the theme to\\n  ohmypi").\\nwhen_to_use: Reconfiguring fa itself — settings, provider, models, memory,\\n  tools, cubes, MCP, redaction, skills access, themes/TUI appearance — on\\n  any host (CLI headless, REPL, app), by editing the YAML config the CLI\\n  persists (themes also via ~/.fah/themes/*.json), never by guessing keys.\\nargument-hint: "[what to configure, e.g. \\\'point project memory at ./memory\\\']"\\nallowed-tools:\\n  - read\\n  - write\\n  - edit\\n  - ls\\n  - bash\\n  - config\\nuser-invocable: true\\ndisable-model-invocation: false\\n---\\n\\n# fa self-configuration\\n\\nYou are reconfiguring fa itself. The config file IS the source of truth: the\\nCLI settings commands (`/provider`, `/tools`, `/approval`, …) are thin\\neditors over the same YAML this skill edits. Edit the file, never invent\\nkeys, verify after every edit, and report what changed and when it applies.\\n\\n## Hard rules\\n\\n1. **Never invent keys.** Unknown top-level keys are ignored silently; strict\\n   sections throw `ConfigException` on unknown keys or bad value types and can\\n   break startup — `mcp:`, `memory:`, `cube:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`,\\n   `images:`, `models.custom` fields, `ttsr:`. The `tools:` section throws on\\n   non-boolean values; unknown TOOL ids only warn (and absent capabilities can\\n   never be force-enabled). Every key you write must come from this document.\\n2. **Never write API key VALUES into config.yaml.** Config carries key NAMES\\n   (`apiKeyName:`) only. Values live in the OS secure store (`/key set`) or the\\n   environment. A key value in YAML is a leaked secret.\\n3. **Preserve the file.** Edit surgically (the `edit` tool, or `write` only for\\n   a file you fully own). Keep comments and unrelated keys byte-identical.\\n4. **Verify after every edit.** Run the `config` tool\\\'s `check` op (or\\n   `fa config check`) and confirm it passes before declaring success. A\\n   broken file must be detected by you, not discovered at next boot.\\n5. **Report scope + application.** Every change report states: which file, which\\n   scope, and whether it applies live or at next boot.\\n\\n## Config layout and precedence\\n\\n| File | Scope | Notes |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `~/.fah/config.yaml` | user (global) | main settings file; loaded by `loadCliConfig` |\\n| `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` | project | only the `memory:`, `cube:`, `tools:`, `spills:` sections are read from here — each wins over the user file |\\n| `<project>/.fah/rules.yaml` | project | TTSR stream rules; project rules win name clashes over the `ttsr:` section |\\n| `<project>/.fah/lsp.json` | project | LSP server map |\\n| `<project>/.fah/packages.yaml` | project | plugin configuration |\\n| `~/.dap/config.json` | user | DAP hub identity/channels (written by the `/settings` hub flow, not YAML) |\\n\\nProject precedence is per section, not per file: `memory:`, `cube:`,\\n`tools:` and `spills:` are loaded separately from the project file\\n(`loadProjectMemoryConfig`, `loadProjectCubeSettings`,\\n`loadProjectToolsConfig`, `loadProjectSpillsConfig`) and win over the\\nsame section in `~/.fah/config.yaml`. All other sections are read from\\nthe user file only.\\n\\nProject sections are strict: a present-but-invalid section throws\\n`ConfigException` at startup. A project `.fah/` that does not exist yet is\\ncreated with a minimal valid file — never leave a half-written YAML behind\\n(write to a temp name and rename, or write the full content in one `write`).\\n\\n## Workflow\\n\\n1. Read the request; identify the topic section below.\\n2. Inspect current state: `config` op `get <key>` / `path` (or read the two\\n   config files — a missing file means defaults, not an error).\\n3. Make the edit: `config` op `set` (preferred — it validates before\\n   writing and preserves the rest of the file byte-for-byte). Fall back to\\n   a surgical file edit (rule 3) only for what `set` cannot express:\\n   removing a key.\\n4. Verify: `config` op `check` (rule 4).\\n5. Report (rule 5), naming the CLI command equivalent that would have made\\n   the same change.\\n\\n## The config tool\\n\\nThe primary editing surface on every host — CLI, desktop app, web, iOS —\\nbecause it needs no shell and no `fa` process. One tool, four ops over the\\nsame core the human CLI verbs wrap:\\n\\n| op | args | effect |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `check` | — | validate both config files with the real parsers; prints errors, warnings, notes and a final `config check: ok` / `config check: failed` |\\n| `path` | — | list the config file locations and whether each exists |\\n| `get` | `key` | the effective value of a dotted key; project scope wins for `memory`/`cube`/`tools` |\\n| `set` | `key`, `value`, `scope`? | surgical single-key write; the edited file is validated BEFORE the write, so an invalid value persists nothing |\\n\\n`set` answers with the file, scope, old → new value, and whether the change\\napplies live or at next boot — echo that in your report (rule 5). `scope`\\ndefaults by key: `memory`/`cube`/`tools` → the project file (created minimal\\nwhen absent), everything else → the user file; pass `global` or `project`\\nto override. Keys come from the topic sections below — the tool rejects\\nunknown top-level keys instead of writing them.\\n`set` also takes LIST-VALUED keys: pass the value as compact JSON (an\\narray or object) and it is rendered as a yaml block — `customProviders`\\nprovider entries are settable this way, e.g. `config` op `set`, key\\n`customProviders`, value\\n`[{"name":"my-llama","apiType":"openai","baseUrl":"http://localhost:11434/v1","modelId":"llama3"}]`.\\n`get` reports list-valued keys as the same compact JSON, so the round\\ntrip is get → edit the JSON → set. A whole list is replaced; to add one\\nentry, get first and re-set the extended list.\\n`get` of a platform-inapplicable key and `set` of one answer\\n`not applicable on this host` with the reason — never write there and\\nnever suggest a file edit as a workaround. The stdio members of an MCP\\nserver (`command`/`args`/`env`) need host process spawning: on web and\\niOS/Android containers they are refused; configure a remote server via\\n`mcp.servers.<id>.url` instead. On a host with no home directory (web)\\nthe global scope is refused for every user-file key — only the project\\nsections (`memory`/`cube`/`tools`) persist there.\\n\\nHuman/script equivalent (thin wrappers over the same service):\\n`fa config check`, `fa config path`, `fa config get <dotted.key>`,\\n`fa config set <dotted.key> <value> [--project|--global]`, and\\n`fa config export-providers [--out <file.fahx>]` (provider-preset export —\\nthe one verb without a config-file write).\\n\\n## Verification\\n\\n`config` op `check` (or `fa config check`) validates both files with the\\nREAL section parsers and prints named diagnostics — this is the mandatory\\nfinal step of every edit:\\n\\n- **What check reports as errors** (non-zero exit / `config check: failed`):\\n  yaml syntax errors, strict-section schema errors (`mcp:`, `memory:`,\\n  `cube:`, `tools:`, `providerTimeouts:`, `skills:`, `images:`, `roles:`,\\n  `ttsr:`, `models.custom`, `fabric:`), and bad scalar types — each naming\\n  file+section.\\n- **Warnings**: unknown top-level keys (the runtime silently ignores them;\\n  the check does not — a typo must not survive) and dead project-file keys.\\n- **At next boot, semantic errors in strict sections are FATAL**:\\n  `invalid ~/.fah/config.yaml: <named diagnostic>` — the process refuses to\\n  start rather than boot a broken config. A passing check is what stands\\n  between your edit and that.\\n- **YAML syntax errors remain silent at RUNTIME** (an unparseable file falls\\n  back to defaults) — `check` is the only place they are reported, which is\\n  why it is mandatory.\\n- **Live re-read surfaces**: in a running REPL, `/tools reload` and\\n  `/mcp reload` re-read their sections immediately and print the parse\\n  error instead of applying it — use them as the live check when a REPL\\n  exists.\\n- Runtime objects keep the last good config when a reload fails (the failed\\n  section never half-applies), so a loud reload error means "nothing changed".\\n\\n## CLI parity map\\n\\nEvery settings command below has a config-file equivalent documented in this\\nskill. If a new settings command appears in the CLI without a section here,\\nthis skill has rotted — flag it in your report.\\n\\n| CLI | Section |\\n|---|---|\\n| `/provider`, `/providers` | [Provider & keys](#provider--keys) |\\n| `/model`, `/models`, `/model-edit` | [Models & roles](#models--roles) |\\n| `/memory` | [Memory](#memory) |\\n| `/tools` | [Tool availability](#tool-availability) |\\n| `/cube` | [Cubes](#cubes) |\\n| `/mcp` | [MCP servers](#mcp-servers) |\\n| `/redact` | [Redaction](#redaction) |\\n| `/skills` | [Skills access](#skills-access) |\\n| `/approval`, `/allow` | [Approval](#approval) |\\n| `/mode`, `/code`, `/architect`, `/review` | [Mode](#mode) |\\n| `/theme` | [Theme](#theme) |\\n| `/settings` | [Settings hub](#settings-hub) |\\n\\n<!-- parity: /provider /providers /model /models /model-edit /memory /tools /cube /mcp /redact /skills /approval /allow /mode /code /architect /review /theme /settings -->\\n\\nThe `fa config check|path|get|set` verbs and the `config` tool share their\\nconfig-file equivalent with the topic sections above (see\\n[The config tool](#the-config-tool)); the parity test pins every verb\\nalongside the slash commands.\\n\\n## Provider & keys\\n\\n<!-- parity: /provider /providers -->\\n\\nUser file, top-level keys:\\n\\n```yaml\\nprovider: openai-completions   # openai-completions | anthropic | google | dial | minimax | zai\\nmodel: openai/gpt-4o-mini      # model id sent to the provider\\nbaseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1\\n```\\n\\nSaved custom endpoints (the `/provider custom` flow persists here):\\n\\n```yaml\\ncustomProviders:\\n  - name: my-llama             # non-empty, unique\\n    apiType: openai            # openai | anthropic | google | dial | openrouter\\n    baseUrl: http://localhost:11434/v1\\n    modelId: llama3            # non-empty\\n    keyName: MY_KEY            # optional: env/secure-store NAME, never the value\\n    authMethod: apiKey         # apiKey | sso | jwt (optional)\\n```\\n\\nApplies: a direct YAML edit takes effect at next boot. `/provider <name>\\n[baseUrl] [token]` switches the live session too.\\nKeys: never inline values (rule 2). Key resolution order — environment value,\\nthen endpoint-scoped secure-store entry (`FA_KEY_<HOST>`), then legacy env-name\\nstore entries. `/key set|delete` manages the store and has NO config.yaml\\nequivalent — that is deliberate.\\n\\n## Models & roles\\n\\n<!-- parity: /model /models /model-edit -->\\n\\nUser file. The active model is the `model:` top-level key (above). Optional\\nsections:\\n\\n```yaml\\nroles:                         # intent → ordered fallback chain\\n  default:\\n    - openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4\\n    - provider: openai         # or a map entry:\\n      model: gpt-4o\\n      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY   # optional; also baseUrl, contextWindow, maxTokens\\n      connectTimeoutMs: 45000       # optional per-entry watchdog override\\n      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000  #   (slow local model recipe, see below)\\n      thinkingLevel: high       # optional: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max\\n                                # (xhigh/max fold to high) — reasoning request\\n  smol: [openrouter/openai/gpt-4o-mini]   # roles: default, smol, slow, plan, subagent, memory\\nmodelOverrides:                # scope chains to path prefixes\\n  - path: ~/work/acme\\n    roles:\\n      plan: [anthropic/claude-opus-4-5]\\nretry:                         # chain fallback policy\\n  retriesPerEntry: 2           # + baseDelayMs, maxBackoffMs, maxWaitMs, keyBackoffMs\\nproviderTimeouts:              # GLOBAL fallback: only these two keys\\n  connectTimeoutMs: 180000\\n  streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000\\nagent:                         # strict: only contextWindowCap (issue #273)\\n  contextWindowCap: 262144     # owner context cap; min 16384 = the compaction reserve\\nimages:                        # session image registry (strict): send-once\\n  registry: true               # kill switch — false = byte-for-byte legacy\\n  maxPerRequest: 20            # per-request unique-image cap (default 20)\\nmodels:                        # media slots + named custom models\\n  slots:\\n    vision:\\n      providerKind: openai-completions\\n      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1\\n      modelId: gpt-4o\\n      apiKeyName: OPENAI_API_KEY\\n  custom:\\n    fast:\\n      provider: openai\\n      baseUrl: https://api.openai.com/v1\\n      model: gpt-4o-mini\\n      contextWindow: 128000    # + maxTokens, input\\n```\\n\\nScoped provider timeouts (issue #1554): `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`\\nare valid on `roles:` chain entries, `customProviders:` entries, and\\n`models.custom:` entries. Per field, the first level that declares a value\\nwins — **role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry >\\nglobal `providerTimeouts:` > built-in default** (connect 180 s, idle 300 s;\\nhard sanity bound 1 h). Configs without the keys behave byte-identically.\\nSlow-local-model recipe: on the role entry that pins the local endpoint set\\nonly `streamIdleTimeoutMs` ≈ 2× the model\\\'s worst silent prefill stretch —\\nthe cloud providers in the same config keep the global watchdog untouched,\\nand the stall line names the override (`idle window 1800s (role default\\noverride)`) so a wide window never reads as a hang.\\n\\nMedia slot names (exact): `imageGeneration`, `audioTts`, `musicGeneration`,\\n`videoGeneration`, `vision`, `transcription`. A slot without an override falls\\nback to the main connection.\\n\\nCLI equivalents: `/model <id>` switches the active model (a\\n`models.custom.<name>` switches provider+endpoint+model in one step);\\n`/models config` displays this section, `/models set <slot> <model>\\n[baseUrl]` and `/models remove <slot>` edit `models.slots`;\\n`/model-edit [contextWindow|maxTokens <n>]` overrides token limits for the\\nsession (persist per chain via `roles:` entries instead). Role edits apply at\\nnext boot; `/model` applies live.\\n\\n## Provider queue\\n\\nProject or user file section; the `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE` env var carries\\nthe same JSON list and WINS over both files (issue #418). The ordered\\nfailover chain replaces the main model: the first healthy entry serves,\\na dead provider hands over loudly to the next, the winner sticks for\\nthe session (RAM-only, never persisted), and cooled-down entries\\nre-enter rotation:\\n\\n```yaml\\nprovidersQueue:\\n  - provider_type: openai-completions\\n    provider_config:\\n      model: moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6\\n      baseUrl: https://gate.example/v1\\n      apiKeyEnv: OPENAI_API_KEY\\n  - provider_type: anthropic\\n    provider_config:\\n      model: claude-sonnet-4-6\\n      apiKeyEnv: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\\n```\\n\\n`apiKeyEnv` names the ENV indirection — a key VALUE never lives in the\\nyaml. CLI equivalent: `/providers queue list|add|remove|move|test`;\\nedits persist to the winning scope\\\'s file and go live from the next\\nturn. App Settings carries the same editor (env scope is read-only\\nthere).\\n\\n## Memory\\n\\n<!-- parity: /memory -->\\n\\nThe long-term memory location. `memory:` may live in the user file or the\\nproject file — project wins.\\n\\n```yaml\\nmemory:\\n  projectPath: ./memory        # inside the repo; committed with it\\n  userPath: ~/memory           # or a user-level store\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/memory` shows stats, `/memory maintain` runs consolidation —\\nneither edits paths; the section is the only way to set them. The live memory\\ncontroller re-reads the section (project resolution via `loadProjectMemoryConfig`),\\nso a path change applies without restart.\\n\\n## Tool availability\\n\\n<!-- parity: /tools -->\\n\\n`tools:` maps a tool id (or `mcp:<server>`) to on/off. Scopes, deepest wins\\nper key; the host\\\'s hard capability floor can never be overridden on:\\n\\n1. global — `~/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`\\n2. project — `<project>/.fah/config.yaml` `tools:`\\n3. session — `.tools/<sessionId>.yaml` next to the session file\\n4. runtime — `--tools` flag / `FA_TOOLS` env (this run only)\\n\\n```yaml\\ntools:\\n  web_search: false\\n  mcp:\\n    fs: true                   # nested mcp: == mcp:<server> keys\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/tools enable|disable <id> [global|project|session]` writes\\nthe matching scope file; `/tools` lists every id with its deciding scope;\\n`/tools reload` re-reads all scopes live. Disabled tools are hidden from the\\nmodel and tombstoned at execution. Edits apply live after a reload.\\n\\n## Cubes\\n\\n<!-- parity: /cube -->\\n\\nSandbox profile selection. `cube:` may live in the user or project file\\n(project wins). Manifests live in `<project>/.fah/cubes/<name>.yaml`.\\n\\n```yaml\\ncube:\\n  enabled: true\\n  config: .fah/cubes/strict.yaml   # path to the cube manifest\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/cube use <name|path>` switches, `/cube off` disables,\\n`/cube list` lists manifests, `/cube reload` re-reads. Applies live via\\n`/cube`; a YAML edit applies at next boot (explicit `--cube`/`--cube-config`\\nflags beat both files).\\n\\n## MCP servers\\n\\n<!-- parity: /mcp -->\\n\\nStrict section — unknown shapes throw `ConfigException`. User file only.\\n\\n```yaml\\nmcp:\\n  toolCallTimeoutMs: 60000\\n  servers:\\n    fs:                        # stdio server\\n      command: npx\\n      args: [-y, "@modelcontextprotocol/server-fs", /tmp]\\n      env: {KEY: value}\\n    docs:                      # remote server\\n      url: https://example.com/mcp\\n      transport: streamable-http   # or sse\\n      headers: {Authorization: "Bearer \\${DOCS_TOKEN}"}\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/mcp` prints per-server status, `/mcp reload` re-reads the\\nconfig live (boot never blocks on MCP). Applies live after `/mcp reload`;\\nconnects lazily in the background.\\n\\n## Redaction\\n\\n<!-- parity: /redact -->\\n\\nUser file `redact:` section (issue #24 layered pipeline):\\n\\n```yaml\\nredact:\\n  enabled: true\\n  blockMode: false             # deny credential-file reads outright\\n  layers:                      # per-layer toggles (priority order in docs/redaction.md)\\n    pii: true\\n  allowlist:                   # regex patterns that survive redaction (git SHAs, UUIDs)\\n    - "[0-9a-f]{40}"\\n  toolAllow: [bash]            # when non-empty, only these tools are redacted\\n  toolDeny: [web_fetch]        # never redacted; wins over toolAllow\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/redact on|off`, `/redact block on|off`, `/redact stats`,\\n`/redact layers`. The command toggles the live pipeline; the section is the\\ndurable form written back when the CLI persists config. Redaction is\\nlive-mutable — no restart needed either way.\\n\\n## Compaction\\n\\nContext-hiding engine choice (issue #148). User or project file (project\\nwins):\\n\\n```yaml\\ncompaction:\\n  engine: structured           # structured (default) | classic (rollback)\\n```\\n\\n`structured` (the default since issue #287) hides records in place behind\\none-line addressable markers (`compact_expand` restores any id or range\\nunder a per-turn token budget); `classic` keeps the lossy summary\\ncompaction — the legacy 1.0 rollback, selected through Settings →\\nCompaction (the app) or an explicit yaml/flag choice. Runtime override:\\n`fa --compaction-engine classic`; resolution is\\nflag > project > global > the structured default. Applies at\\nthe next compaction.\\n\\n## Skills access\\n\\n<!-- parity: /skills -->\\n\\nUser file section governing third-party skill discovery\\n(`.claude/`, `.github/skills`, `.codex/`):\\n\\n```yaml\\nskills:\\n  access: granted              # ask | granted | denied\\n  disableShellExecution: false # strip !`cmd` injections from third-party skills\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/skills access ask|granted|denied` (and the `/skills` menu).\\n`/skills import` copies third-party skills into `.fah/skills`. Applies live on\\nre-discovery.\\n\\n## Approval\\n\\n<!-- parity: /approval /allow -->\\n\\nUser file top-level keys:\\n\\n```yaml\\napprovalMode: yolo             # always-ask | write | yolo | unattended\\nallowedTools:                  # always-allow list (exec tier still honors critical patterns per mode)\\n  - web_fetch\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/approval <mode>`, `/allow <tool>` — both persist to these\\nkeys. Applies at next boot (the running session keeps its live mode).\\n\\n## Power\\n\\nUser file section (issue #325, reworked in #326). Sleep prevention for\\nlive runs — by default ONE assertion PER RUN (acquired when the run\\ngoes in flight, released when it settles), so the machine cannot\\nidle/sleep out from under a long run but CAN sleep while the agent\\nidles between turns:\\n\\n```yaml\\npower:\\n  sleepPrevention: idle # off | idle | display | system (default idle)\\n  hold: per-run # per-run | session (default per-run)\\n```\\n\\nLevels are cumulative: `idle` keeps the system from idle-sleeping\\n(macOS `caffeinate -i`), `display` also keeps the display awake\\n(`-i -d`), `system` also blocks AC system sleep and declares the user\\nactive (`-i -d -s -u`). `hold: session` is the explicit opt-in that\\nholds from session start to exit instead (always-on deployments).\\nmacOS spawns `caffeinate -w <fa pid>` (exits with fa — never\\norphaned), Linux tries `systemd-inhibit` best-effort, other platforms\\nno-op. A failed assertion is a warning, never a crash.\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/power` (level + hold + held state). Applies at next\\nboot.\\n\\n## Subagents heartbeat\\n\\nUser file section (issue #383). While a background subagent runs, the\\nparent receives a periodic status digest through the steering channel —\\nage, provider requests/tokens, last activity, and a\\n`healthy | stalled | no-progress-since-spawn` classification per running\\nchild. A child with no provider activity for `stallMinutes` (or that\\nnever issued a request at all) gets a loud `⚠ STALLED` flag with the\\nsuggested `task_status → task_cancel → respawn` action; the flag\\nescalates to `⚠⚠` at twice the threshold:\\n\\n```yaml\\nsubagents:\\n  heartbeatMinutes: 10 # digests cadence; 0 disables the heartbeat\\n  stallMinutes: 20 # quiet window before a stall flag; 0 disables flags\\n```\\n\\nZero running children → no digest; completion notices are unchanged.\\nConfig changes apply at the next digest tick — no restart required.\\n\\n## Mode\\n\\n<!-- parity: /mode /code /architect /review -->\\n\\nUser file top-level key:\\n\\n```yaml\\nmode: code                     # code | architect | review\\n```\\n\\nCLI equivalent: `/mode <name>` or the `/code`, `/architect`, `/review`\\nshortcuts — they switch live AND persist this key.\\n\\n## Theme\\n\\n<!-- parity: /theme -->\\n\\nThe TUI palette is data, never code. `/theme` lists every available theme\\n(built-ins first, then user themes) with a swatch preview; `/theme <name>`\\nswitches immediately and persists the choice; `/theme reset` returns to\\nthe default.\\n\\nConfig equivalent — the persisted theme name:\\n\\n```yaml\\ntui:\\n  theme: default   # a built-in name or a user theme file stem\\n```\\n\\nBuilt-in names: `default` (the historical site palette — teal `#5eead4`,\\nindigo `#818cf8`), `catppuccin`, `nord`, `dracula`, `ohmypi-dark`,\\n`ohmypi-light`, `pi`.\\n\\nUser themes live in `~/.fah/themes/<name>.json`; the file stem is the\\ntheme name, and a user theme can never shadow a built-in (a clashing file\\nname is skipped with a boot note). The JSON holds a `"roles"` object mapping ROLE names to hex colors\\n(`"#rgb"` or `"#rrggbb"`): `accent`, `accent2`, `muted`, `highlight`,\\n`success`, `warning`, `error`, `border`, `focusBorder`, `userMessageBg`.\\nEvery role is optional — a missing role inherits the default theme for\\nthat slot. Unknown role names, invalid hex, or broken JSON produce a\\nnamed error (file, role, line) at load time, never a crash.\\n\\nApplies: `/theme <name>` switches the live session in one frame; a direct\\nYAML edit takes effect at next boot. Asked to create a theme from a\\ndescription, write the JSON file, then apply it with `/theme <name>` and\\nconfirm the swatch line with the user. Asked for a palette "like X" where\\nX is unknown, ask two or three palette questions first — never invent one\\nsilently.\\n\\n### Compaction report detail\\n\\nBy default an auto-compaction fold prints ONE short marker line\\n(`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the internal\\ncheckpoint summary stays in the session file (reachable via\\n`compact_expand`) and out of the console. To render the full report block\\n(records + fenced summary) and the live summarizer stream on headless\\nruns, opt in:\\n\\n```yaml\\ntui:\\n  showCompactionDetails: true\\n```\\n\\nThe manual `/compact` command always renders the full block. Applies at\\nnext boot.\\n\\n## Prompts, TTSR & A2A\\n\\nThe remaining user-file sections (all global scope):\\n\\n```yaml\\nprompts:                        # prompt overrides: prompt id → text or @file\\n  concise: "Answer in one short paragraph."\\nttsr:                           # tool-schema reduction (TTSR)\\n  enabled: true\\n  contextMode: keep             # keep | discard\\n  repeatMode: after-gap         # after-gap | once\\na2a:                            # remote Agent2Agent endpoints\\n  servers:\\n    peer:\\n      url: https://peer.example:8080\\n      token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value]}      # env-resolved at boot — never a literal secret\\nfabric:                         # host discovery announcements (read-only:\\n  capabilities:                 # written by hosts, never user-edited)\\n    - name: yoclip.render\\n      description: Render the open project to MP4\\n```\\n\\n`a2a` servers are remote-only (a `url`, like remote MCP servers), so they\\nconfigure fine on process-less hosts. A `token` is an `\\${ENV}` reference\\nresolved at boot; config `check`/`set` keep the token text literal, so an\\nunset variable surfaces when the agent boots, not as a config error.\\n\\n## Settings hub\\n\\n<!-- parity: /settings -->\\n\\n`/settings` is an interactive hub over the surfaces above (provider, model,\\napproval, cube, keys, MCP, DAP hub). It has no single config equivalent —\\neach arm edits the section documented for it. DAP hub settings are the one\\nsurface NOT in config.yaml: the hub flow writes `~/.dap/config.json`\\n(identity keys, channels). Configure DAP through the hub flow or see\\ndocs/dap.md; never hand-edit the DAP files while a hub client is running.\\n\\n## Example invocations\\n\\n- `point project memory at ./memory` → Memory section: `config` op `set`,\\n  key `memory.projectPath`, value `./memory` (project file is the default\\n  scope — created minimal if missing), then `check`, then report live\\n  application.\\n- `switch us to provider X` → Provider & keys: `config` op `set` for\\n  `provider:` (and `baseUrl:`) in the user file — global scope is the\\n  default for these keys; report next-boot application and the `/provider`\\n  equivalent.\\n\\n- `add custom provider Y and switch to it` → Provider & keys: `config` op\\n  `get customProviders`, `config` op `set customProviders <extended JSON\\n  list>` (see the config-tool section), then `set provider openai-completions`,\\n  `set model <entry modelId>`, `set baseUrl <entry baseUrl>`; verify with\\n  `check`, report next-boot application and the `/provider` equivalent.\\n- `disable web_search for this project` → Tool availability: `config` op\\n  `set`, key `tools.web_search`, value `false` (project scope by default);\\n  report live after `/tools reload` semantics (host REPL) or next re-read.\\n- `configure cube backend Z` → Cubes: `config` op `set` for the `cube:`\\n  keys (project file for a repo default) and reference the manifest in\\n  `.fah/cubes/`.\\n\\n## Output\\n\\n<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->\\n\\nConsole-output behavior flags (gh-1198 + gh-1433), user file. Today one\\nkey — the live thinking stream for CLI line-mode runs: with\\n`streamThinking: true` (or the `--stream-thinking` flag, which wins for\\nthe run), thinking deltas print dimmed and live like the TUI\\\'s, so ssh\\nsessions show the model\\\'s reasoning as it happens. The default `false`\\nkeeps the interactive line-mode byte shape and prints a periodic\\n`… reasoning Ns` liveness line instead while a provider request sits\\nsilent — the same waiting cadence the tool-liveness lines use\\n(`waiting.toolLivenessSeconds` / `toolLivenessTickSeconds`; `0` disables).\\n\\nSince gh-1433 this key decides the INTERACTIVE faces only: a headless\\n`fa -p` run streams thinking and text by default (the log is the UI, no\\nflags needed). `--no-stream-thinking` silences thinking for one headless\\nrun (the reasoning liveness line returns), and `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy`\\nreverts the whole headless face to the pre-gh-1433 byte shape for edge\\nhosts that parse the log. Rendered deltas — thinking AND streamed text,\\non every face — pass through the redaction pipeline at render time since\\ngh-1433: a registered secret echoed in a delta is masked live, so\\nbyte-pin tests for interactive `--stream-thinking` sessions must assume\\nredacted deltas whenever redaction is enabled (default).\\n\\n```yaml\\noutput:\\n  streamThinking: false # interactive line mode only; headless runs stream by default\\n```\\n\\nApplies at next boot (the flag applies to its own run).\\n\\n## Tool-result spilling\\n\\n<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->\\n\\nOversized tool results spill to `.fah/spills/<sessionId>/<n>.txt` and the\\nsession keeps a bounded preview + path + size stats (issue #678). Tolerant\\nparse: unknown keys and mistyped scalars surface as `[spills]` notes at\\nboot, never boot failures. `enabled: false` or `threshold: 0` = legacy\\nbehavior (nothing spills):\\n\\n```yaml\\nspills:\\n  enabled: true # kill switch; false = byte-identical legacy\\n  threshold: 8192 # chars above which a tool result spills\\n  headChars: 2000 # preview head bound (chars)\\n  tailChars: 2000 # preview tail bound (chars)\\n```\\n\\nApplies at next boot.\\n\\n## Session retention\\n\\n<!-- parity: none (boot config only) -->\\n\\nThe `sessions:` section (gh-1746) is the opt-in disk hygiene policy for\\nthe sessions root: when the total on disk crosses `maxTotalBytes`, a\\nboot sweep deletes whole session units oldest-last-used-first. Live\\nsessions (fresh heartbeats), named sessions, and sessions younger than\\n`minAgeDays` are always exempt — and with no `sessions:` section at all\\nnothing is EVER auto-deleted (byte-identical legacy boot). Tolerant\\nparse: unknown keys become notes, never boot failures. ### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e9216f9a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch
re-creates all three as `io`/`cleanEnv`/`cleanRoot` with identical expressions.
Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a
`--cwd` handling the other forgets). Same for the `FileSessionPresenceStore`
wiring, which is copied verbatim from the repair branch.

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could
   at least cross-check `header.id == sessionId` (filename-derived) so a
   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.

### 7. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e9216f9a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the clean branch duplicates the env/io/root construction already in scope**

Inside `if (sessionList != null)` the enclosing block already built `io`
(`_TerminalCliIO(headless: true)`), `listEnv` (`LocalExecutionEnv(cwd: …)`), and
`sessionRoot` (`parsed.sessionRoot ?? _defaultSessionRoot()`) — the clean branch

Reuse the enclosing locals so the two verbs cannot drift (e.g. one gaining a

### 1. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:7573d2dc` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

## Fixed — header `cwd` is validated before it can drive any delete

Added `isSafeSpillCwd()` to `lib/src/session_retention.dart`: a header cwd must be non-empty, absolute (POSIX `/…` or Windows `X:\…`/`X:/…`), and free of `..` segments on either separator. The guard runs in `_scanSlugDir` right after header parse — a unit with an unsafe cwd is skipped **with a note** (`retention: skipped <path> — unsafe header cwd "…" (E4)`) and never becomes a sweep candidate, so ONE guard covers both the usage walk's `_dirBytes` measurement and the sweep's `_removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/<sid>')`. Fail closed: a corrupted/truncated/planted header disqualifies the unit entirely rather than risking an outside-root delete.

Tests (test/session_retention_test.dart, "E4 path escape" group): relative `../../etc` cwd and absolute `/work/../evil` cwd are never measured nor deleted (the outside spill trees survive, the notes explain the skip), and a safe absolute cwd still sweeps normally (no over-blocking).

### 2. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:e6e73fef` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

🚨 **BLOCKING: the boot sweep can delete the very session this process is about to open (data loss)**

`_retentionBootCheck()` runs as the first statement of `_initializeSession()`,
BEFORE `config.sessionName` is resolved (line 421+), and the sweeper here gets no
`currentSessionId`. Presence registration happens much later
(`agent_cli.dart:1918`, `_registerLivePresence()` after the session loads), so at
sweep time the resume target has no presence row.

Reachable data-loss sequence:

1. `fa --session <id>` — the resume form the exit hint itself prints for
   unnamed sessions (`_sessionNameMatches` resolves ids: "ids must resolve too").
2. The target is old (> `minAgeDays`), unnamed, not live, root over cap →
   **this boot's own sweep deletes its transcript + sidecars**
   (AC3's "current session" exemption is unimplementable as wired — the id is
   knowable from args but never passed).
3. `_sessionNameMatches` then finds nothing and `_createSession(name: <id>)`
   silently creates a fresh empty session — the user sees their marathon
   workspace "open" with zero history.

`keepNamed: true` (default) protects only sessions whose name resolves from the
transcript; resume-by-id of an unnamed session — and any resume with
`keepNamed: false` — is unprotected. The E2 mid-sweep presence re-check cannot
help: this process registers presence only after the sweep.

Fix: resolve the resume target before sweeping and pass it as
`currentSessionId` (or exempt it explicitly), e.g. resolve
`config.sessionName` via `_sessionNameMatches` first and hand the sweeper the
match id; only then run `enforceAtBoot()`.

Also note: `_retentionBootCheck` has no test coverage (see the test-gap thread),
which is exactly why this seam shipped broken.

### 3. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:f0a17f8f` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `header.cwd` is unvalidated and drives a recursive `removeTree`**

`cwd` comes from the first line of the session file — data a corrupted,
truncated, or maliciously planted session header controls. The sid component is
guarded (`isSafePathSegment`), but `cwd` is interpolated raw:

```dart
await _removeTree('$cwd/.fah/spills/${session.sessionId}');
// → _fs.remove(dir, recursive: true, force: true)
```

A header carrying `cwd: "../../x"` or `cwd: "/"` makes the sweep recursively
delete an arbitrary `<path>/.fah/spills/<sid>` tree outside any root. The
symlink check in `_removeTree` does not stop plain directory traversal.

The usage walk (`_dirBytes('${header.cwd}/.fah/spills/<sid>')`) reads the same
unvalidated path — lower stakes, but the delete path needs a guard:

```dart
final resolved = _safeJoinUnder(header.cwd, '.fah/spills', session.sessionId);
// reject: not absolute, contains '..' segments, or empty
```

Require absolute, `..`-free cwds before measuring/deleting spills; skip with a
note otherwise. Please also consider validating in `_headerFacts` at parse time
so one guard covers both uses.

### 4. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:9394bd6a` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `sessionIdFromSessionPath` duplicates `JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath`**

This helper is a verbatim copy of the private
`JsonlSessionRepo._sessionIdFromPath` (lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:754):
same `<timestamp>_<sessionId>.jsonl` split, same null rules. Two parsers for the
same encoding can drift (e.g. if the filename scheme ever gains a segment).

Either extract one shared top-level function (session_repo's copy can delegate
to it) or add a cross-reference comment on both sides pinning them together.

### 5. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:623be55b` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: `SessionDiskUsage.name` is dead surface, and `_SessionHeaderFacts.id` is parsed but unused**

Two related nits in the walk:

1. `SessionDiskUsage.name` ("when already known") is never populated —
   `_scanSlugDir` constructs every usage without `name:`, and `_nameOf` resolves
   lazily into a separate set. The field is always null in practice.
2. `_headerFacts` requires `decoded['id'] is String` but never uses it. It could

   mismatched/foreign header is treated as unidentified instead of counted as a
   sweepable unit keyed by its filename.

Either wire them (name from the header probe; id as an identity check) or drop
the unused surface.

### 6. `pr_discussions.md:ai-teammate:2026-10-22:60e996b0` — **ai-teammate** (`pr_discussions.md`) on 2026-10-22

💡 **SUGGESTION: the AC4 blocker note names every exempt session, not the ones actually holding the cap**

When the root remains over cap, this loop adds ALL non-deleted sessions as
blockers — including 1 KB "young" sessions that have nothing to do with the
overflow — and the header line then claims "N exempt session(s) hold X". With a
large store the note becomes noise that hides the real blockers (usually the one
giant live session).

Consider naming only the sessions that are actually needed to explain the
overflow (walk blockers largest-first until `held > remaining - cap`), or at
least ordering the printed list by size and capping its length.
